rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. Testing RNA-only with singleprofile and PCA (config_001) isolates the effect of the RNA encoder and profile setting, providing foundational performance metrics. This clarifies whether RNA-only models are viable before exploring more complex multimodal configurations.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation method. It balances exploration (testing multiprofile) and exploitation (using a simpler aggregation method first) to determine if combining multiple profiles improves performance, which is critical for understanding data structure.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) with avgpool aggregation (used in config_002) could further improve accuracy. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder while maintaining the promising multiprofile and avgpool settings, balancing exploration of encoder quality against exploitation of existing multiprofile success.

Existing evidence shows that using multiprofile with scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_005) achieves 0.65 accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping rna_encoder=scvi_n200 and multiprofile) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method on a strong baseline, balancing exploitation of the RNA-only multiprofile direction with exploration of architectural changes.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation (config_006) achieves 0.6529 accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to the more advanced scgpt RNA encoder with the same transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current best setup and exploration of a promising new component.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with multiprofile settings and transformer aggregation (config_006: 0.652970) outperform others. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation (vs. scvi_n200 in config_006) could yield better performance, isolating the effect of RNA encoder choice while keeping profile and aggregation consistent. This balances exploitation of aggregation method benefits with exploration of RNA encoder alternatives.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting achieve the highest accuracy (0.6529). This experiment tests combining scvi_n200 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder (a strong image backbone) using avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, which isolates the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation (using proven RNA encoder) with exploration (adding image modality) to determine if multimodal approaches can surpass the current RNA-only best.

The existing evidence shows that rna-only models (e.g., config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.65297). Multimodal models like config_030 (0.6315) lag behind, but changing fusion methods (concat vs. weighted) could improve performance. This experiment tests whether weighted fusion in multimodal setups (scvi_n200 + resnet50) outperforms concat, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It balances exploration of multimodal potential and exploitation of promising components (scvi_n200, resnet50).

Existing evidence shows multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 achieve high accuracy (config_031: 0.6776). This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation (vs. avgpool in config_031) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It's a logical extension of the top-performing configuration and could either confirm or refine the optimal approach before exhausting the budget.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033: 0.713087) outperform others. This experiment tests whether replacing ResNet50 with the more advanced ImageNet ViT-L encoder (config_039) further improves accuracy in this high-performing setup. It isolates the impact of image encoder choice while maintaining proven aggregation/fusion strategies, addressing key uncertainty about ViT's efficacy in this domain.
